slides.title: Immunization CDS (ImmDS + HALO)
slides.subtitle: Version 0.1.0 · Topic Reference for community discussion
slides.speaker_notes: This is an intentionally incomplete discussion artifact, not an approved standard or final design.

slides.title: A forecast needs more than age and vaccination history

content.text: Patient and assessment date
Immunization history
Optional Contextual Conditions
An identifiable executable Knowledge Base
Visible limitations and provenance

slides.speaker_notes: The Topic Reference makes all five parts visible so systems can exchange a result without hiding assumptions.

slides.title: One bounded request, one coherent Knowledge Base, a transparent response
slides.speaker_notes: Diagram: Requesting system sends assessment date, patient, immunization history, and optional context to a CDS service. The service applies one Knowledge Base. The response contains evaluations, recommendations, transparency, and provenance.

slides.title: Contextual Conditions make important forecast inputs explicit

content.text: The requesting system supplies the assertion
Omission means unknown, not No
The service reports whether it recognized and used the condition
The detailed concept remains in the related Contextual Conditions Topic Reference

slides.speaker_notes: Examples include pregnancy, relevant immune status, travel, or maternal RSV vaccination. These are operational CDS inputs, not arbitrary diagnoses inferred by the forecast operation.

slides.title: Published guidance and executable rules are related—not identical

content.text: Guidance source
Publishes clinical recommendations and intent
Currently called Schedule Authority; the term is provisional
Knowledge Base
Identifiable executable rules applied by a CDS service
May operationalize one or more sources of guidance

slides.speaker_notes: The distinction answers whose guidance is relevant versus which executable rules actually ran.

slides.title: Clients select a Knowledge Base—not a runtime mix of authorities
slides.speaker_notes: Diagram: one or more guidance publishers feed a predefined Knowledge Base; the client selects the Knowledge Base; the CDS service executes it; the response identifies what ran and preserves useful provenance.

slides.title: Transparency answers two different questions

content.text: This forecast call
What was used, ignored, unsupported, incomplete, or blocked?
Service capability
Which vaccines, Knowledge Bases, and conditions can the service generally support?

slides.speaker_notes: Patient-specific response transparency and general capability discovery have different scopes and lifecycles.

slides.title: Version 0.1.0 makes the unsettled work visible

content.text: Replace or confirm Schedule Authority terminology
Settle Knowledge Base identity, versioning, and provenance
Define minimum transparency and capability contracts
Reconcile the FHIR binding with the Contextual Conditions model
Choose the compatibility path from original ImmDS

slides.speaker_notes: The goal is useful reaction and prioritization, not premature closure.

slides.title: Use the Topic Reference as the shared home for the next discussion

content.text: Correct the conceptual model
React to the two diagrams
Prioritize the open questions
Feed accepted changes back into canonical Markdown
